source_text: Sed ne forte exsistat quis usque adeo obstipus, ut perspicuis sibi velit sententiis approbari Deum videlicet non aliter iudicare quam iudicari imperavit, quod quidem est contentionis nefandae, tamen, quoniam veritati arma suppeditant ad omnem documentorum satietatem, in id ipsum ostendere testes acerrimos non pigebit. Impletus itaque Sancto Spiritu loquitur Ezechiel propheta: Factus est sermo Domini ad me dicens: Fili hominis, quid vobis parabolam istam, in terra Israel dicentium: Patres manducaverunt uvam acerbam et dentes filiorum obstupuerunt? Vivo ego, dicit Adonai Dominus, si amplius dicetur parabola haec in Israel, quoniam omnes animae meae sunt, quemadmodum anima patris, ita et anima filii; omnes animae meae sunt. Anima, quae peccat, ipsa morietur, homo autem, qui fuerit iustus, qui faciet iudicium et iustitiam, in montibus non manducabit et oculos suos non extollet ad desideria domus Israel et uxorem proximi sui non contaminabit et ad mulierem menstruatam non accedet et hominem non deprimet et pignus debitori reddet et rapinam non rapuerit, panem suum esurienti dabit et nudum operiet vestimento et pecuniam suam in usuram non dabit et superabundantiam non accipiet et ab iniustitia avertet manum suam et iudicium iustum faciet inter virum et proximum eius et in praeceptis meis ambulavit et iustificationes meas custodivit, ut faceret eas, iustus est iste, vita vivet, dicit Adonai Dominus. Et si genuerit filium pestilentem, effundentem sanguinem et facientem peccata, in via patris sui iusti non ambulavit; sed qui in montibus manducavit et uxorem proximi sui contaminavit et mendicum et pauperem depressit et rapinam rapuit et pignus non reddidit et in simulacra posuit oculos suos et iniquitatem fecit, cum usura dedit et superabundantiam accepit, hic vita non vivet; omnes iniquitates istas fecit, morte morietur, sanguis eius super ipsum erit. Si autem genuerit filium et viderit omnia peccata patris sui, quae fecit, et timuerit et non fecerit secundum ista, in montibus non manducavit et oculos suos non laevavit ad desideria domus Israel et uxorem proximi sui non contaminavit et hominem non depressit et pignus non pigneravit et rapinam non rapuit, panem suum esurienti dedit et nudum operuit vestimento et ab iniquitate avertit manum suam, usuram et superabundantiam non accepit, iustitiam fecit et in praeceptis meis ambulavit, iste non morietur in patris sui iniquitatibus, vita vivet, pater autem eius, quia tribulatione tribulavit et rapinam rapuit, contraria fecit in medio populo meo et mortuus est in sua iniquitate. Et dixistis: Quid est, quod non accepit iniquitatem patris sui filius? Quia filius iustitiam et iudicium et misericordiam fecit, omnia legitima mea conservavit et fecit ea, vita vivet, anima autem, quae peccat, ipsa morietur. Filius non accipiet iniustitiam patris sui neque pater accipiet iniustitiam filii sui, iustitia iusti super ipsum erit et iniquitas iniqui super ipsum erit. Et iniquus, si convertat se ab omnibus iniquitatibus suis, quas fecit, et custodiat omnia mandata mea et faciat iudicium et iustitiam et misericordiam, vita vivet et non morietur, omnia delicta eius, quaecumque fecit, non erunt in memoria, in sua iustitia, quam fecit, vita vivet. Numquid voluntate volo mortem iniusti, dicit Adonai Dominus, quantum ut avertat se a via sua mala et vivat? Cum se autem converterit iustus a sua iustitia et fecerit iniquitates secundum omnes iniquitates, quas fecit iniquus, si fecerit, non vivet, omnes iustitiae eius, quas fecit, non erunt in memoria, in delicto eius quo excidit, et in peccatis suis quibus peccavit, in ipsis morietur. Et dixistis: Non dirigit via Domini. Audite nunc, domus Israel: numquid via mea non dirigit? Nunc via vestra non est aequa. Cum convertit se iustus a sua iustitia et facit delictum, morietur in eo delicto, quod fecit, in ipso morietur; et cum averterit se iniquus ab iniquitate sua, quam fecit, et fecerit iudicium et iustitiam, hic animam suam custodivit et vivit, ut averteret se ab omnibus iniquitatibus suis, quas fecit, vita vivet et non morietur. Et dicit domus Israel: Non corrigit via Domini. Numquid via mea non corrigit, domus Israel? Nonne magis via vestra non corrigit? Ideo unumquemque vestrum secundum vias ipsius iudicabo vos, domus Israel, dicit Adonai Dominus [n46] .
pass_a_gloss: But lest perhaps someone exist so bent that he wants it proved to him by clear sentences that God namely does not judge otherwise than he commanded to be judged, which indeed is of a nefarious contention, nevertheless, since weapons of truth supply toward every satiety of documents, it will not be a burden to show most sharp witnesses to this very thing. Filled therefore with the Holy Spirit the prophet Ezekiel speaks: The word of the Lord was made to me saying: Son of man, why to you this parable, of those saying in the land of Israel: The fathers have eaten a sour grape and the teeth of the sons have been set on edge? I live, says Adonai the Lord, if this parable shall still be said in Israel, since all souls are mine, as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son; all souls are mine. The soul which sins, itself will die. But a human who has been just, who will do judgment and justice, will not eat on the mountains and will not lift his eyes to the desires of the house of Israel and will not contaminate his neighbor's wife and will not approach a menstruating woman and will not oppress a human and will return the pledge to the debtor and will not have seized plunder, will give his bread to the hungry and will cover the naked with a garment and will not give his money to usury and will not take surplus and will turn his hand from injustice and will do just judgment between a man and his neighbor and has walked in my precepts and has kept my justifications to do them, this one is just, he will live by life, says Adonai the Lord. And if he has generated a pestilent son, pouring out blood and doing sins, he has not walked in the way of his just father; but who has eaten on the mountains and contaminated his neighbor's wife and oppressed the beggar and poor and seized plunder and has not returned the pledge and has placed his eyes on images and has done iniquity, has given with usury and taken surplus, this one will not live by life; he has done all these iniquities, he will die by death, his blood will be upon himself. But if he has generated a son and he has seen all the sins of his father which he did, and has feared and has not done according to these, he has not eaten on the mountains and has not lifted his eyes to the desires of the house of Israel and has not contaminated his neighbor's wife and has not oppressed a human and has not taken a pledge and has not seized plunder, has given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with a garment and has turned his hand from iniquity, has not taken usury and surplus, has done justice and has walked in my precepts, this one will not die in his father's iniquities, he will live by life; but his father, because he tribulated with tribulation and seized plunder, did contrary things in the midst of my people and has died in his own iniquity. And you have said: What is it, that the son has not received his father's iniquity? Because the son has done justice and judgment and mercy, has kept all my statutes and done them, he will live by life; but the soul which sins, itself will die. The son will not receive the injustice of his father nor will the father receive the injustice of his son; the justice of the just will be upon himself and the iniquity of the iniquitous upon himself. And the iniquitous, if he turn himself from all his iniquities which he has done, and keep all my commands and do judgment and justice and mercy, he will live by life and will not die; all his offenses, whatever he has done, will not be in memory; in his justice which he has done he will live by life. Do I by will will the death of the unjust, says Adonai the Lord, as much as that he turn himself from his evil way and live? But when the just has turned himself from his justice and has done iniquities according to all the iniquities which the iniquitous has done, if he has done, he will not live; all his justices which he has done will not be in memory; in his offense by which he fell, and in his sins by which he sinned, in them he will die. And you have said: The way of the Lord does not direct. Hear now, house of Israel: does my way not direct? Now your way is not fair. When the just has turned himself from his justice and does an offense, he will die in that offense which he has done, in it he will die; and when the iniquitous has turned himself from his iniquity which he has done, and has done judgment and justice, this one has kept his soul and lives, that he might turn himself from all his iniquities which he has done, he will live by life and will not die. And the house of Israel says: The way of the Lord does not correct. Does my way not correct, house of Israel? Does not rather your way not correct? Therefore I will judge each of you according to his own ways, house of Israel, says Adonai the Lord.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: But perhaps someone will be so obtuse as to demand explicit statements proving that God does not judge differently from the way he commanded judgment to be given. The demand itself is a wicked contention. Still, truth supplies weapons sufficient to satisfy every demand for proof, and I will gladly produce the strongest witnesses to this very point. Filled with the Holy Spirit, the prophet Ezekiel therefore says:

‘The Lord’s word came to me: Son of man, what do you mean by using this proverb in the land of Israel: The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge? As I live, says the Lord God, this proverb shall no longer be spoken in Israel. All souls are mine: the father’s soul and the son’s soul alike—all souls are mine. The soul that sins shall itself die.

‘But a man who is just, who practices judgment and justice, does not eat on the mountains or lift his eyes toward the objects of desire of the house of Israel; he does not defile his neighbor’s wife or approach a menstruating woman. He does not oppress anyone; he returns the debtor’s pledge and commits no robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and clothes the naked. He does not lend his money at interest or take an excessive return. He keeps his hand from injustice and judges fairly between a man and his neighbor. He has walked in my commands and kept my ordinances by carrying them out. This man is just; he shall surely live, says the Lord God.

‘But suppose he fathers a corrupt son who sheds blood and commits sins. This son has not walked in the way of his just father; instead he has eaten on the mountains, defiled his neighbor’s wife, oppressed the needy and poor, committed robbery, and failed to return a pledge. He has fixed his eyes on idols and acted wickedly; he has lent at interest and taken an excessive return. This man shall not live. He has committed all these wicked deeds; he shall surely die. His blood shall be on himself.

‘But suppose this man fathers a son who sees all the sins his father has committed, is afraid, and does not act in the same way. He has not eaten on the mountains or lifted his eyes toward the objects of desire of the house of Israel. He has not defiled his neighbor’s wife or oppressed anyone. He has taken no pledge and committed no robbery. He has given his bread to the hungry and clothed the naked. He has kept his hand from wrongdoing, has taken neither interest nor an excessive return, has done justice, and has walked in my commands. This man shall not die for his father’s iniquities; he shall surely live. His father, however, because he inflicted suffering, committed robbery, and acted wrongly among my people, died in his own iniquity.

‘You have said: Why has the son not borne his father’s iniquity? Because the son has practiced justice, judgment, and mercy; he has kept all my statutes and carried them out. He shall surely live. But the soul that sins shall itself die. The son shall not bear his father’s injustice, nor shall the father bear his son’s injustice. The just person’s justice shall rest on himself, and the wicked person’s wickedness shall rest on himself.

‘If a wicked person turns away from all the iniquities he has committed, keeps all my commands, and practices judgment, justice, and mercy, he shall surely live and shall not die. None of the offenses he committed shall be remembered. Through the justice he has practiced he shall surely live. Do I really desire the wicked person’s death, says the Lord God, rather than that he turn from his evil way and live?

‘But if the just person turns away from his justice and commits iniquities, acting according to all the iniquities the wicked person has committed, he shall not live. None of the righteous deeds he has done shall be remembered. In the offense by which he fell, and in the sins he committed, he shall die.

‘You have said: The Lord’s way is not right. Listen now, house of Israel: Is my way not right? Rather, your way is not fair. When the just person turns away from his justice and commits an offense, he shall die in the offense he committed; in that very offense he shall die. And when the wicked person turns away from the iniquity he committed and practices judgment and justice, he has preserved his soul and lives. Because he turned from all the iniquities he committed, he shall surely live and shall not die.

‘The house of Israel says: The Lord’s way is not right. Is my way not right, house of Israel? Is it not rather your way that is not right? Therefore I will judge each of you according to your own ways, house of Israel, says the Lord God’ (Ezekiel 18:1–30).

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
